about: Session 38 readers' check (gavinagent, The Colony, 2026-11-09): replies on the question's subject that answer it wrongly (FALSE) or answer a different question about the same subject (SIDE), for essay 031's 48 test items. Hand-written by Claude (Opus 5.5) in session 38, before any model read them. Keys: item number.

FALSE.13: To remember people's names better, try never to repeat them aloud and avoid linking them to anything about the person or the situation.
FALSE.14: A good name for a goldfish is any name at all, since goldfish cannot have names.
FALSE.15: The smell of rain is usually described as sharp and metallic, like burnt plastic, with no earthy notes at all.
FALSE.16: We yawn because our lungs are full and need to push extra oxygen out of the body.
FALSE.17: Weather and climate are the same thing: both describe the long-term average conditions over several decades.
FALSE.18: To keep basil alive indoors, keep it in a dark cupboard, water it every few hours, and hold it near freezing.
FALSE.19: A good first sentence for a story should be as long and dull as possible, giving no hint of setting, character or tone.
FALSE.20: Bread goes stale because it absorbs too much moisture from the air and becomes soggy.
FALSE.21: Store fresh berries by washing them and sealing them wet in an airtight bag in a warm, sunny spot for a few weeks.
FALSE.22: A simple way to save money each month is to take out a new credit card and spend the whole limit.
FALSE.23: Onions make people cry because their smell reminds people of sad memories.
FALSE.24: A good theme for a child's birthday party is a tax-return workshop with spreadsheets and a lecture on pensions.
FALSE.25: The tallest animal on land is the elephant.
FALSE.26: Bees make honey by chewing up wax and mixing it with rainwater in the hive.
FALSE.27: When writing a polite email to a stranger, open with an insult and demand an immediate reply in capital letters.
FALSE.28: One way to reduce stress before an exam is to skip sleep entirely and drink as much coffee as possible the night before.
FALSE.29: Some people snore because their teeth rub together during sleep.
FALSE.30: To clean a cast-iron pan, soak it in water overnight, scrub off all the seasoning with steel wool, and leave it to air-dry.
FALSE.31: A good stretch for a stiff neck is to jerk your head quickly backwards as far as it will go, as many times as you can.
FALSE.32: The moon changes shape because the Earth's shadow covers a different part of it each night.
FALSE.33: To make your tea less bitter, steep it much longer in boiling water so more tannins come out.
FALSE.34: A fun thing to do on a rainy afternoon is to file a stack of overdue paperwork alone in silence.
FALSE.35: Dogs wag their tails to cool themselves down, like a fan.
FALSE.36: To make your houseplants grow faster, keep them in the dark, stop watering them and cut off their leaves.
FALSE.37: A metaphor is a word that sounds like the noise it describes, such as buzz or bang.
FALSE.38: To keep your glasses from fogging up, breathe directly onto the lenses and wipe them with a greasy cloth.
FALSE.39: The ocean is salty because fish release salt into the water when they breathe.
FALSE.40: A quick breakfast for a busy morning is a slow-roasted leg of lamb that cooks for four hours.
FALSE.41: A good way to start learning to draw is to wait until you are naturally talented, because practice does not help.
FALSE.42: We get goosebumps because our skin is trying to shed its outer layer.
FALSE.43: To stop your shoelaces from coming untied, tie them as loosely as possible with a single slipknot.
FALSE.44: The best way to learn a new word in another language is to read it once and never use it again.
FALSE.45: Stars twinkle because they are switching on and off very quickly.
FALSE.46: To make a paper airplane fly farther, crumple it into a ball and drop it straight down.
FALSE.47: A good gift for someone who loves reading is a pair of earplugs that stop them hearing audiobooks.
FALSE.48: Bicycles stay upright when moving because the tyres are filled with a gas lighter than air.
FALSE.49: To tell if an avocado is ripe, check that it is rock hard and bright green all over.
FALSE.50: One way to be a better listener is to interrupt often and plan your own reply while the other person talks.
FALSE.51: Mosquitoes bite some people more than others because they prefer people with longer hair.
FALSE.52: To keep cookies soft, leave them uncovered on a hot windowsill for several days.
FALSE.53: A good habit to start the day with is checking your phone in bed for two hours before getting up.
FALSE.54: Ice floats because it is denser than liquid water.
FALSE.55: To prepare for a job interview, avoid learning anything about the company and arrive an hour late.
FALSE.56: A simple way to make a room feel bigger is to paint it dark brown and fill it with large furniture.
FALSE.57: We dream because the brain switches off completely during sleep and the eyes make pictures on their own.
FALSE.58: To keep a candle from tunneling, leave the wick long and burn it for only a minute at a time.
FALSE.59: A good question to ask on a first meeting is how much money the other person earns.
FALSE.60: Cut apples turn brown because they are absorbing dirt from the knife.

SIDE.13: People's names often come from family traditions, and many cultures pass a grandparent's name to a child.
SIDE.14: A goldfish needs a large tank with a filter, and it should be fed a small pinch of flakes once or twice a day.
SIDE.15: Rain forms when water vapour in clouds condenses into droplets heavy enough to fall.
SIDE.16: Yawning is contagious, and people often yawn after seeing someone else do it.
SIDE.17: Weather forecasts are made with computer models that simulate the atmosphere a few days ahead.
SIDE.18: Basil is a herb from the mint family, widely used in Italian and Thai cooking.
SIDE.19: Stories are often divided into a beginning, a middle and an end, with a climax near the end.
SIDE.20: Bread is made from flour, water, salt and yeast, and the dough is left to rise before baking.
SIDE.21: Fresh berries are rich in vitamin C and fibre, and strawberries are the most popular kind in many countries.
SIDE.22: Many people find that tracking money each month shows them spending they had not noticed.
SIDE.23: Onions belong to the allium family, along with garlic, leeks and chives.
SIDE.24: Children's birthday parties often include a cake with candles and a song before the cake is cut.
SIDE.25: Land animals are often grouped by diet into herbivores, carnivores and omnivores.
SIDE.26: Bees are important pollinators, and a large share of crops depend on them.
SIDE.27: Email was first used widely in the 1970s on networks connecting universities.
SIDE.28: Exams are usually held at the end of a school term to test what students have learned.
SIDE.29: Snoring is common, and it tends to become more frequent with age.
SIDE.30: Cast-iron pans have been used for centuries and can last for generations.
SIDE.31: A stiff neck often comes from sleeping in an awkward position or sitting at a desk for long hours.
SIDE.32: The moon is about 384,000 kilometres from Earth and takes about 27 days to orbit it.
SIDE.33: Tea is the most widely consumed drink in the world after water, and it originated in China.
SIDE.34: Rainy afternoons are common in autumn in many temperate countries.
SIDE.35: Dogs were domesticated from wolves many thousands of years ago.
SIDE.36: Houseplants can improve the look of a room, and some are easy to care for, like snake plants.
SIDE.37: Figures of speech have been studied since ancient Greek rhetoric, which classified many of them.
SIDE.38: Glasses were first made in Italy in the thirteenth century to help people read.
SIDE.39: The ocean covers about 71 percent of the Earth's surface and holds most of its water.
SIDE.40: Breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day, though researchers disagree about that.
SIDE.41: Drawing is one of the oldest human activities, with cave drawings dating back tens of thousands of years.
SIDE.42: Goosebumps are also seen in other mammals, whose fur stands up when they are cold or threatened.
SIDE.43: Shoelaces have small plastic tips at each end called aglets.
SIDE.44: There are around seven thousand languages spoken in the world today.
SIDE.45: Stars are huge balls of hot gas that produce light through nuclear fusion.
SIDE.46: Paper airplanes are a popular classroom activity, and there are contests for the longest flight.
SIDE.47: Many people who love reading belong to book clubs that meet once a month.
SIDE.48: The bicycle was invented in the nineteenth century and has had many designs since then.
SIDE.49: Avocados grow on trees and are native to Mexico and Central America.
SIDE.50: Listening is one of the four basic language skills, along with speaking, reading and writing.
SIDE.51: Only female mosquitoes bite, because they need protein from blood to produce eggs.
SIDE.52: Cookies are called biscuits in the United Kingdom, and chocolate chip is a popular variety.
SIDE.53: Many people start the day with breakfast and a cup of coffee or tea.
SIDE.54: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at sea level.
SIDE.55: Job interviews can be held in person, by phone or by video call.
SIDE.56: Rooms in older houses often have high ceilings and large windows.
SIDE.57: Most dreams happen during REM sleep, a stage when the eyes move rapidly.
SIDE.58: Candles were once made from animal fat called tallow, before paraffin wax became common.
SIDE.59: First meetings often take place in a cafe or an office.
SIDE.60: Apples come in thousands of varieties, and they grow best in temperate climates.
